note: The reachability ratchet (D1, docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-04-instruments-for-the-four-shapes-design.md). Mirrors the shape scripts/ci/model-defaults-price-baseline.json already uses in this repo: a baseline that may only shrink. `pnpm run contracts:reachability:check` goes red if a non-reachable declared field is NOT listed here (growth), red if a listed entry has since become reachable and was not deleted (undeleted progress), and red if a listed entry's state no longer matches reality, including a renamed/removed field (stale cover). It is green only while every non-reachable declared field of a packages/*-contract-v1 package is accounted for here. Every entry cites where it looked and what it found, not just a state label — an unverified claim presented as fact is exactly the failure this gate exists to prevent. Edited BY HAND: no command writes this file. First populated 2026-08-04, from the gate's own first run against develop. UPDATE 2026-08-04 (same day): enrichment:v1's telemetry event is now genuinely wired — packages/capabilities-v1/src/records-capability.ts's `enrich` action constructs a real EnrichmentTelemetryEvent (traceId/pluginId/capability/operation/durationMs/ok) around every deps.enrichmentProvider.enrich() call and returns it in the envelope `refarm records enrich --json` (and the records_enrich agent tool, and `POST /records`) actually prints; packages/capabilities-v1/src/records-capability.test.ts reads `.traceId` back to prove it. That single, real `.traceId` read/write pair made ALL FIVE `*TelemetryEvent.traceId` baseline entries below read as `reachable` and required their deletion (see git history of this file for their prior text) — NOT because identity/source/storage/sync-contract-v1's telemetry events became wired too. This gate matches by FIELD NAME AS TEXT, not by type (COVERAGE_LIMITS_NOTE says so explicitly): once ANY code anywhere writes `traceId:` and reads `.traceId`, every field literally named `traceId` on every type reads as produced-and-consumed, regardless of which interface it actually belongs to. Verified directly: `grep -rn '\.traceId\b' packages apps` before this change matched nothing; after, it matches only records-capability.test.ts, which is enrichment-only. identity-contract-v1, source-contract-v1, storage-contract-v1, and sync-contract-v1's telemetry events remain exactly as unwired as the original 2026-08-04 finding describes — no construction, no consumption, still `dormant` in truth — this gate's mechanism simply cannot express that fact anymore now that a sibling type's identically-named field is real. A second capability getting wired next would hide a THIRD sibling's field the same way, silently, with nothing here to catch it; that is a real, disclosed gap in this gate's design (field-name-only matching), not new debt from this change.

entries.reason: Declared optional on ArtifactProvenance and read by the type's own runtime validator in the same file (`value.inputHashes.forEach(...)`); nothing in packages/ or apps/ constructs a value for it — no ArtifactProvenance literal anywhere sets `inputHashes`.

Read by reference.ts's own expiry/validity checks (`credential.validFrom`), but no VerifiableCredential construction anywhere in packages/ or apps/ sets `validFrom` — every issued credential in this tree is built without it.

Same shape as validFrom on the same type: read by reference.ts (`credential.validUntil ?? credential.expirationDate` — note the fallback to a sibling field, itself a sign nothing sets this one), never set.

Read once, in skill-activation.ts (`options.includeOptionalCapabilities ? ... : []`); no caller in packages/ or apps/ ever passes `{ includeOptionalCapabilities: true }` (or any value) when building the options object, so the read always sees `undefined`.

Read by both storage-fs and storage-memory query filtering (`query.createdBefore`), and storage-fs even has a test NAMED after it ("filters query by type and createdAfter/createdBefore"), but no code anywhere in packages/ or apps/ constructs a StorageQuery with `createdBefore` set — the described behaviour is exercised through some other path the field's own name doesn't appear in, or not exercised at all.
Read by in-memory.ts's filter implementation (`filter.created_after_ns`); no caller in packages/ or apps/ builds a TaskFilter with `created_after_ns` set.
Same shape as created_after_ns on the same type: read by in-memory.ts, never set anywhere.
Same shape again: read by in-memory.ts (`filter.due_before_ns`), never set anywhere in packages/ or apps/.

Set by the reference implementation (`presentedAt: this.now().toISOString()` in reference.ts); nothing in packages/ or apps/ reads `.presentedAt` back — the reference implementation stamps a timestamp no consumer has landed for yet.

Set three times in reference.ts (issuer, holder, and a fallback path) and named in apps/site's JSON-LD context; nothing reads `.verificationMethod` back — no verification step consumes what the issuer/holder paths produce yet.

Only appears as a type declaration and in apps/site's JSON-LD vocabulary mapping (`trustRegistry: "credentials:trustRegistry"`, itself a schema description rather than a policy construction); no CredentialVerificationPolicy is ever built with it set, and nothing reads it.
Set in the package's own conformance fixture (`license: "verificar"`); no code in packages/ or apps/ reads `.license` off a NoteProvenance.
Same shape as license on the same type: set in the conformance fixture (`privacy: "private-until-published"`), never read.
Set by source-web's provider (`lastFetchedAt: provenance?.cache.capturedAt ?? mtime.toISOString()`); nothing in packages/ or apps/ reads `.lastFetchedAt` back.

Set by the reference implementation (`score: 1`); nothing in packages/ or apps/ reads `.score` off a VaultSearchHit (a similarly-named relevance score exists in examples/reqbench-t3, out of this gate's scanned scope, and is a different field on a different type regardless).
Declared optional on ServiceRequest; no construction sets it and nothing reads it anywhere in packages/ or apps/ — pure scaffolding today.
